capabilities.title: Fatigue and durability
capabilities.description: Investigate behaviour under repeated loading, characterise fatigue response and compare life predictions with experimental results.

capabilities.title: Mechanical characterisation
capabilities.description: Study the mechanical response of engineering materials and components. Previous research includes polymer composites, hybrid joints and the influence of temperature on material behaviour.

capabilities.title: Joints and structural integrity
capabilities.description: Connect measurements and computational analysis to assess welded components and mechanical joints, including residual stresses and fatigue response.

capabilities.title: Numerical–experimental validation
capabilities.description: Combine finite element analysis with mechanical measurements to examine model predictions. Research experience includes strain, vibration and temperature measurements and component-level correlation.

capabilities.title: Engineering data and methods
capabilities.description: Process experimental data, develop scientific software and compare analytical or computational methods. Reproducible datasets and documented algorithms support interpretation and model validation.

measurement_context.title: Material and joint response
measurement_context.description: Previous studies document static and fatigue characterisation of materials and joints. The specimen, loading conditions and required measurements define the feasibility of a new campaign.

measurement_context.title: Strain, vibration and temperature
measurement_context.description: These measurement categories feature in existing research. Sensors, acquisition settings, operating ranges and facility access must be confirmed for each investigation.

measurement_context.title: Model correlation and data processing
measurement_context.description: Experimental results can be compared with finite element and analytical models, using scientific programming to evaluate predictions and document the analysis.

equipment.title: StepLab axial–torsional electrodynamic machine
equipment.description: Electrodynamic test system for controlled axial and torsional fatigue loading of round and flat specimens. Frequency depends on the loading mode and specimen.
equipment.status_note: Specified limits depend on specimen, fixture and operating mode; they are not simultaneous guarantees.
equipment.image_alt: StepLab machine behind its transparent protective enclosure
equipment.image_caption: StepLab experimental testing equipment. The photograph does not identify a particular capacity variant.

equipment.title: Schenck servo-hydraulic axial–torsional system
equipment.description: Servo-hydraulic axial–torsional testing, with a separate internal-pressure actuator for tubular specimens. The historical group inventory reports typical machine frequencies of approximately 10–20 Hz.
equipment.status_note: Force, torque, pressure and frequency limits depend on the arrangement and must not be assumed simultaneously attainable.
equipment.image_alt: Two large Schenck hydraulic actuators on a steel experimental test structure
equipment.image_caption: Schenck hydraulic actuators in the mechanical-testing laboratory.

equipment.title: Rumul resonant fatigue-testing machines
equipment.description: The historical facilities inventory documents two resonant systems used for high-cycle fatigue and fatigue crack-growth investigations on compatible specimens.
equipment.status_note: Historical equipment ratings only; confirm the present machine inventory and availability before a study.
equipment.image_alt: Green Rumul resonant fatigue-testing frame showing its grips and load train
equipment.image_caption: Rumul resonant fatigue-testing machine; the photographed capacity variant is not identified.

equipment.title: MTS servo-hydraulic uniaxial systems
equipment.description: The earlier group facilities inventory records two uniaxial servo-hydraulic machines for monotonic and cyclic material testing.
equipment.status_note: Published historical ratings, not a statement that both systems are currently available.

equipment.title: StepLab electromechanical machine
equipment.description: Smaller-capacity electromechanical equipment for compatible axial and cyclic test configurations.
equipment.status_note: Available loading modes and frequency depend on the selected specimen and fixture.

equipment.title: Reconfigurable structural test bench
equipment.description: A configurable bench equipped, in the arrangement described by the group, with three Schenck hydraulic actuators for component-level investigations, including welded joints and vehicle frames.
equipment.status_note: A historical facilities description refers to a full-scale bench with up to seven actuators. This is not an additional claim for the present three-actuator arrangement.
equipment.image_alt: Wide modular heavy steel structural testing bench with a grid of threaded mounting positions
equipment.image_caption: Reconfigurable structural test bench for tailored experimental setups.

equipment.title: Structural vibration and dynamics
equipment.description: Experimental shaker arrangements support vibration measurements, dynamic characterisation and suitable vibration-fatigue campaigns. Historical group activities also include robotic laser-vibrometer modal measurements.
equipment.status_note: Do not transfer the StepLab 250 Hz limit to separate vibration equipment. Modal instrumentation availability is project-dependent.
equipment.image_alt: TIRA electrodynamic shaker with an experimental component mounted on a test fixture
equipment.image_caption: Vibration-testing arrangement with a TIRA shaker and experimental fixture.

equipment.title: Thermal and environmental conditioning
equipment.description: Temperature-controlled equipment for suitable fatigue, creep and creep–fatigue investigations, depending on machine compatibility and test fixtures.
equipment.status_note: The climatic chamber is one device, described in conjunction with compatible StepLab configurations; ranges cannot necessarily be combined with maximum mechanical loads.

equipment.title: Specimen preparation and metrology
equipment.description: In-house CNC turning, milling and tooling for round, flat, notched and tubular specimens. Surface characterisation includes contact/optical roughness measurements and Vickers hardness testing.
equipment.status_note: The older group webpage additionally records SEM/optical microscopy, Charpy and hole-drilling measurements; their current availability is unconfirmed.

equipment.title: FLIR X6901sc high-speed infrared camera
equipment.description: High-speed infrared temperature-field imaging for experimental thermal measurements. Values shown are manufacturer specifications, not confirmed performance for every laboratory setup.
equipment.status_note: Optics, calibration, filters and operating settings determine achievable measurements. No unverified lock-in or thermoelastic method is implied.
equipment.image_alt: FLIR X6901sc infrared camera in its protective carrying case
equipment.image_caption: FLIR X6901sc high-speed mid-wave infrared camera.
